findings.title: Working-hours check compares the same value twice and uses inverted logic
findings.body: In checkIfIsAvailable, `start` and `end` are both computed as `slotStartTime.hour()*60 + slotStartTime.minute()`. The slot's end time is never used, so a slot that starts inside working hours but ends after them passes. The `.find` returns true when the slot is OUTSIDE a single working-hours entry. With several entries for the same day (multiple users or split hours), a slot inside one range but outside another is rejected. Working hours are also compared in UTC minutes against the UTC day, so ranges crossing midnight in UTC are mishandled. Net effect: availability is wrongly rejected or accepted.

findings.title: Object identity comparison is always false
findings.body: `dayjs(a) === dayjs(b)` compares two distinct object references, so it is never true. The intended zero-length override check (start equals end) is dead code. A day blocked by an override with start equal to end would not be treated as unavailable by this branch.

findings.title: Date override matching is by UTC calendar day and the offset sign is questionable
findings.body: The override's start is shifted by minus the organizer's utcOffset (taken at that instant) and its date string is compared to the slot's UTC date. This mixes organizer-local and UTC days. Overrides that span midnight in UTC, or whose UTC date differs from the organizer's local date, will not match the slots they apply to. An override that exists on a day never blocks slots after `date.end` on a neighbouring UTC day. Only the first matching override is considered, because `find` stops at the first true result. With multiple overrides on one day (the same user's several ranges, or different users'), a slot inside one range can be rejected because another range returned true first.

findings.title: Override offset uses the invitee's current-day timezone and wraps minutes modulo 24h
findings.body: The offset is computed from `dayjs(override.start.toString())`. `Date.toString()` is a locale string, so parsing it is non-ISO and can be unreliable and lossy. The shifted start/end are then reduced to hour*60+minute, which wraps at midnight. When the shift crosses a day boundary, endTime can end up smaller than startTime and the override produces no slots. The filter on activeOverrides still compares override.start in UTC to the invitee's day, so it is not timezone-adjusted. Also, `override.timeZone` may be undefined, which makes `.tz(undefined)` use the local timezone.

findings.title: Timezone test expects identical output, so it does not verify the fix
findings.body: The new test requests the +6:00 timezone but expects the same UTC slots as for +5:30, and the comment says so. The PR claims override slots should shift with the invitee timezone. The test only checks that slots are keyed by UTC date, so it passes without exercising the changed offset logic. There is also no test for the fixed-host round-robin date override scenario that the PR targets.
